title: Organically synthesized porous carbon anodes for sodium-ion batteries: high capacity, fast charging, and dendrite suppression
content: Here we report the first evaluation of organically synthesized porous carbon (OSPC) as a sodium-ion anode material, addressing a key limitation of current battery technology. Sodium-ion batteries offer cheap, abundant, and sustainable materials for the energy transition but remain limited by anode performance. Present state-of-the-art niobium-based materials or hard carbon achieve, respectively, a capacity of up to 120 mAh g−1 at a high C rate (5C) or, under typical conditions, a capacity of 300 mAh g−1 at low C rates (0.1C), with no one material performing well at both low and high charging rates. OSPCs are a form of carbon related to conjugated microporous polymers that have shown strong anode performance in lithium-ion systems. OSPC-0 anode material exhibits a competitive capacity across the full charging rate range with 250 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, 120 mAh g−1 at 3.4C, and a capacity of 80 mAh g−1 at 12C, with the added advantage of showing resistance to the formation of dangerous sodium metal dendrites. These results position OSPC-0 as a competitive alternative anode material combining high capacity, fast-charging capability, and dendrite resistance in a single material.
